sc_index_zero_start.title: Where does string indexing start?
sc_index_zero_start.prompt: In Python, what index gives the first character of a string?
sc_index_zero_start.hint: Python's first normal index is zero.

help.concept: String indexing is zero-based, so the first character is at index `0`.
help.hint_1: Index `1` refers to the second character.
help.hint_2: Index `-1` refers to the last character.

sc_slice_end_rule.title: How slice end positions work
sc_slice_end_rule.hint: A slice includes its start position and excludes its end position.

help.concept: `text[start:end]` begins at `start` and stops immediately before `end`.
help.hint_2: Index `4` is the stopping boundary, not part of the result.

options.a: It gets only the character at index 4
options.b: It gets characters from index 1 through index 4, including both
options.c: It gets characters from index 1 up to, but not including, index 4
options.d: It removes characters from index 1 to index 4

sketch_index_basics.title: Use indexes to get one character
sketch_index_basics.bodyMarkdown:
A string is a sequence of characters. Each character has an index.

Python starts counting at `0`:

```python
word = "python"

print(word[0])
print(word[3])
```

Output:

```text
p
h
```

So:

- `word[0]` is the first character;
- `word[3]` is the fourth character.

Negative indexes count from the end:

```python
print(word[-1])
print(word[-2])
```

Output:

```text
n
o
```

Use a single index when you need exactly one character.

sketch_slice_basics.title: Use a slice to get part of a string
sketch_slice_basics.bodyMarkdown:
A slice returns a substring instead of one character.

The basic form is:

```python
text[start:end]
```

Python includes `start` and stops **before** `end`.

```python
text = "banana"
print(text[1:4])
```

Output:

```text
ana
```

The slice includes indexes `1`, `2`, and `3`, then stops before index `4`.

That end-exclusive rule is important:

```text
start included
end excluded
```

Use a bounded slice such as `[1:4]` when you know both the starting position and the stopping position.

sketch_common_patterns.title: Use open and negative slices for common patterns
sketch_common_patterns.bodyMarkdown:
You can leave out one side of a slice.

```python
text = "banana"

print(text[:3])
print(text[3:])
```

Output:

```text
ban
ana
```

- `text[:3]` starts at the beginning and stops before index `3`.
- `text[3:]` starts at index `3` and continues to the end.

Negative indexes also work inside slices:

```python
code = "ABCD1234"

print(code[-2:])
```

Output:

```text
34
```

Useful patterns include:

- `text[0]` → first character
- `text[-1]` → last character
- `text[:n]` → first `n` characters
- `text[n:]` → everything from index `n` onward
- `text[-n:]` → last `n` characters

A single out-of-range index raises an error, while a slice can safely stop beyond the string's length.
